headline: President Obama creates an emergency board to look into a labor dispute between New Jersey Transit Rail and some of its unionized workers.
what_it_does: This order sets up a Presidential Emergency Board to investigate a dispute between New Jersey Transit Rail and certain employees represented by labor unions. Under federal railroad labor law, such boards study the dispute and make recommendations for settling it. Creating a board also generally delays strikes or lockouts for a set period while the process plays out.

who_it_affects.group: New Jersey Transit Rail employees represented by the unions in the dispute
who_it_affects.how: Their contract dispute will be reviewed by the emergency board, and any strike is generally put on hold during the process.
The agency must take part in the board's investigation, and a lockout is generally put on hold during the process.
Their train service is less likely to be disrupted by a strike while the board does its work.
